task_label: Music theory and listening — Correction and reflection
essential_question: How can understanding music foundations and listening help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to choose a different representation or strategy for active listening, then demonstrate corrected understanding.

Check, revise, or improve work about active listening using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about active listening.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.

materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: This is day 12 of "Music Foundations and Listening". That is unit 3 in grade 5. Today is a correction and reflection about active listening. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Create an annotated listening map and perform or sequence a short rhythmic or melodic piece. Today helps by working on active listening. Your unit also covers steady beat and rhythm, pitch and melody, dynamics and tempo, and form. Today adds real evidence toward your unit project.
primary_task: Go back to your earlier work on active listening and improve it. Do not just replace it. Make a fix-it list. What was not working? Why do you think that happened? What did you change? How can you tell it is better? Keep the old and new side by side. Then look at all the problems together. What do they have in common? Name one thing you will do differently. Honest notes about weak work score full marks here. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about active listening. It is part of "Music Foundations and Listening". Later days in this unit cover other things, like steady beat and rhythm. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about active listening; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 5, finish on your own. Write a reason for each main choice. If there were two ways to do it, say which one you picked and why.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses sound (active listening). You do not have to hear it to do it. You may use a written or drawn version, feel the beat by tapping or watching, or read the notes on paper instead.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting active listening.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for active listening follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for active listening, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for active listening works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of active listening, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking active listening mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply active listening under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on active listening rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
